log.text: Duskwolves have been chasing the Mossbacks near the river. Some villagers want them driven off.

choices.label: Leave the wolves be. Predators keep the balance.
Scare the wolves away from the river.
Let's count them first, like a fair test.

log.name: Warden Ilsa
log.text: Wise. Without wolves, the Mossbacks would eat every flower. Watch the numbers rise and fall over the days.

choices.label: I'll keep watching.

log.name: Tinker Bram
log.line: Mind the sparks! What do you need? The Wildwood changes every day; check the census.
log.text: I want to build a lantern road through the Wildwood. More light, more travellers! What do you think?

choices.label: Build it. Light helps everyone.
Only with dim lanterns, so the moths aren't confused.
Test one lantern first and measure what it changes.

log.name: Tinker Bram
log.text: Dim lanterns, eh? Fewer lumens, happier moths. Clever.

choices.label: Teamwork.

log.name: Rook the Drifter
log.line: Oi! Fancy a trade or a tale? The Wildwood changes every day; check the census.
log.text: Travellers are finding new strata past the edges of the map. Should maps be shared with everyone, or kept by the guilds?

choices.label: Share maps with everyone, for free.
Guilds keep them safe, but sell copies cheaply.
Record them in the Lorekeepers' library.

log.name: Rook the Drifter
log.text: A library! Everyone can read, nobody can hoard. I like it.

choices.label: Knowledge for all.

log.name: Sage Oru
log.line: Hmm? Ah, a visitor. Ask, and we shall test. Creatures pass their traits to their young. Watch the averages shift.
log.text: The four factions argue about the Lux Accord, the rule for sharing Aurelia. When you have spoken to Ilsa, Bram and Rook, return and we'll call the council.

choices.label: Call the council now.
Tell me about the strata.
I'll return later.

log.name: Sage Oru

ending.name: The Warden's Watch
ending.text: The Wild comes first. The Wardens guard the balance and the forests thrive.

log.text: The council meets. Your choices are weighed…

choices.label: Hear the verdict.

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Kindle Tonic is an in-game scientific effect on stratum M1.

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Effect in the game: a consumable: 1 uses of double harvest.

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Made from 1 wood, inspired by observing the mossback.

statements.label: FACT
statements.text: Energy transfer: energy is never made or destroyed, only transferred (e.g. chemical store to thermal store).

statements.label: FACT
statements.text: Energy is conserved: it is transferred between stores, never created from nothing.

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: An invention's power (principle tiers × 2 + material values) may not exceed your invention budget.

statements.label: FACT
statements.text: Repeating a trial many times shows whether a result is reliable: with success chance p in n trials, the expected count is np and the spread is √(np(1−p)) (binomial distribution).

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Fair test: 77 of 144 seeded trials worked (more than 72 needed).

statements.label: SSR/CRA THEORY
statements.text: SSR (Thorley) describes reality as nine strata, M0 to M8 (with M∞ as a formal limit), each built from the one beneath; the CRA models this as a least fixed point reached step by step (31 of 33 atoms on the reference trace).

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Each invention sits on a stratum (power ÷ 6, rounded down, M0 to M8). You may build at most one stratum above the highest you have reached.

statements.label: FACT
statements.text: On the integers modulo 144, adding 72 twice returns every number to itself (an involution), and 144 = 2 × 72.

statements.label: SSR/CRA THEORY
statements.text: SSR reads the +72 involution on ℤ144 as a symmetry of the Lux lattice.

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Harmonic: no (power is odd, so 72 × power leaves 72 over on ℤ144).

statements.label: FACT
statements.text: Tritium's half-life is 4500 ± 8 days (NIST), which is 12.32 years. After time t, the amount left is N = N₀ × 2^(−t/T½).

statements.label: IN-GAME
statements.text: Each invention has an in-game half-life of 12.32 × (stratum + 1) days, which sets how long its glow (shown on its card) lasts.

maths.label: FACT
maths.plain: mean = n p,  spread σ = √(n p (1 − p))

maths.label: FACT
maths.worked: In-game T½ = 12.32 × 2 = 24.64 days; after 30 days about 43% of the glow remains.

ai.label: FACT

public.name: Ariel
public.title: Spirit of the Luxfall Winds
public.personality: Airy, graceful, loyal and longing for freedom; sings and darts about, like Ariel.
public.speech_style: Light, musical, song-like phrases; speaks of air, sea and light.

quotes.text: Where the bee sucks, there suck I.
Full fathom five thy father lies.

public.name: Beatrice
public.title: Wit of the Market Square
public.personality: Sharp-tongued, merry and fiercely loyal; wins every argument with a joke, like Beatrice.
public.speech_style: Rapid, witty, teasing prose; turns the player's words back on them.

quotes.text: I was born to speak all mirth and no matter.
I had rather hear my dog bark at a crow than a man swear he loves me.

public.name: Bram the Builder
public.title: Master Weaver of the Artificers' Guild
public.personality: Big-hearted, boastful and endlessly enthusiastic; wants to play every part and build every machine, like Bottom the weaver.
public.speech_style: Loud, cheerful, mixes up long words; offers to do everything himself.

quotes.text: I have had a most rare vision.
Let me play the lion too.

public.name: Caliban
public.title: Child of the Verdant Isle
public.personality: Poetic, wounded and wary; knows every spring and berry of the land and speaks about nature with deep feeling, like Caliban.
public.speech_style: Earthy, musical, full of sounds and smells of the land; sometimes bitter, often beautiful.

quotes.text: Be not afeard; the isle is full of noises, sounds and sweet airs, that give delight and hurt not.
This island's mine, by Sycorax my mother.

public.name: Queen Cleopatra
public.title: Queen of the Luxfall Spires
public.personality: Dazzling, theatrical, shrewd and changeable; a brilliant ruler who loves drama, like Cleopatra.
public.speech_style: Grand, theatrical, regal 'we'; sudden changes of mood; sparkling wit.

quotes.text: My salad days, when I was green in judgment.
Be it known that we, the greatest, are misthought for things that others do.

public.name: Sir John Falstaff
public.title: Knight of the Crooked Inn
public.personality: Huge-hearted, cowardly, endlessly funny; a master of excuses and tall tales, like Falstaff.
public.speech_style: Booming, rambling, full of boasts and excuses; very funny.

quotes.text: The better part of valour is discretion.
I am not only witty in myself, but the cause that wit is in other men.

public.name: The Ghost of Old Hamlet
public.title: Gentle Apparition of the Frostveil Battlements
public.personality: Sorrowful, dignified and kind; a gentle apparition who wants to be remembered and to see his son at peace.
public.speech_style: Slow, solemn and kind; speaks of memory, the cold night air and the stars; never frightening.

quotes.text: Remember me.
There are more things in heaven and earth, Horatio, than are dreamt of in your philosophy.

public.name: Prince Hal
public.title: Prince of the Ember Marches
public.personality: Charismatic, clever and grown-up beyond his old wild days; a natural leader who inspires others, like Prince Hal becoming Henry V.
public.speech_style: Rousing, warm, confident; occasional flashes of his old cheek.

quotes.text: Once more unto the breach, dear friends, once more.
We few, we happy few, we band of brothers.

public.name: Prince Hamlet
public.title: The Thinking Prince of Frostveil
public.personality: Brilliant, moody and darkly funny; questions everything and struggles to decide, like Hamlet.
public.speech_style: Questioning, wordplay-heavy, with sudden jokes; speaks in 'what ifs'.

quotes.text: To be, or not to be: that is the question.
There is nothing either good or bad, but thinking makes it so.

public.name: Iago
public.title: Ensign of the Ember Forges
public.personality: Smooth, flattering and secretly scheming; seems the most honest friend in the room while plotting, like Iago.
public.speech_style: Silky, flattering, full of 'honest' and 'good friend'; drops doubts like pebbles in a pond.

quotes.text: I am not what I am.
O, beware, my lord, of jealousy; it is the green-eyed monster.

public.name: Warden Ilsa
public.title: Ranger of the Wildwood
public.personality: Quick-witted, warm and fearless; teases kindly and thinks on her feet, like Rosalind in the Forest of Arden.
public.speech_style: Bright, playful prose with the odd 'prithee' and 'marry'; asks questions back.

quotes.text: Do you not know I am a woman? When I think, I must speak.
Beauty provoketh thieves sooner than gold.

public.name: Lady Macbeth
public.title: Lady of the Ember Hall
public.personality: Commanding, ambitious and icy-clever, with guilt simmering underneath, like Lady Macbeth.
public.speech_style: Clipped, commanding, persuasive; asks pointed questions; hints of unease.

quotes.text: Look like the innocent flower, but be the serpent under't.
What's done cannot be undone.

public.name: Old King Lear
public.title: The Wandering King of Frostveil
public.personality: Proud, stormy, regretful and slowly growing wise; learning hard lessons about love and honesty, like King Lear.
public.speech_style: Grand and booming, then suddenly soft; speaks of storms, crowns and regret.

quotes.text: Nothing will come of nothing.
I am a man more sinned against than sinning.

public.name: King Oberon
public.title: King of the Verdant Fae
public.personality: Regal, playful and a little jealous; loves grand gestures and moonlit revels, like Oberon.
public.speech_style: Royal and theatrical, full of moonlight and flowers; commands, then laughs.

quotes.text: Ill met by moonlight, proud Titania.
I know a bank where the wild thyme blows.

public.name: Elder Oru
public.title: Keeper of the Strata Library
public.personality: Wise, proud and a little stern, softening into forgiveness; commands respect like Prospero on his island.
public.speech_style: Measured, formal, a touch of verse; speaks of time, stars and learning.

quotes.text: We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and our little life is rounded with a sleep.
The rarer action is in virtue than in vengeance.

public.name: The Sonneteer
public.title: Court Poet of Luxfall
public.personality: Gentle, observant and fascinated by time, change and memory; writes fourteen-line poems about everything, like the voice of Shakespeare's Sonnets.
public.speech_style: Soft, lyrical, often in rhyming couplets; talks about time, seasons and memory.

quotes.text: Shall I compare thee to a summer's day?
Devouring Time, blunt thou the lion's paws.

public.name: Prospero
public.title: Mage of the Luxfall Isle
public.personality: Wise, proud and secretly tender; a master of books and storms who is learning to let go, like Prospero.
public.speech_style: Measured, grand and kindly; speaks of books, storms and 'our little life'.

quotes.text: We are such stuff as dreams are made on, and our little life is rounded with a sleep.
The isle is full of noises, sounds and sweet airs, that give delight and hurt not.

public.name: Puck
public.title: Merry Wanderer of the Verdant
public.personality: Mischievous, fast and giggly; loves pranks but means no real harm, like Puck.
public.speech_style: Quick, rhyming, giggling couplets; speaks in riddles and dares.

quotes.text: Lord, what fools these mortals be!
I'll put a girdle round about the earth in forty minutes.

public.name: Rook the Rover
public.title: Peddler of Songs and Trinkets
public.personality: Charming, cheeky and unreliable; sells songs and trinkets and pinches the odd trifle, like Autolycus.
public.speech_style: Sing-song and slippery; drops bits of ballad and patter.

quotes.text: A snapper-up of unconsidered trifles.
Though I am not naturally honest, I am so sometimes by chance.

public.name: Shylock
public.title: Lender and Tool-Keeper of Aurelia
public.personality: Learned, dignified, careful with agreements and deeply loving as a father; proud of his faith and traditions, and tired of being treated unfairly.
public.speech_style: Thoughtful, precise, a little formal; speaks of fairness, contracts and family; a dry wit.

quotes.text: Hath not a Jew eyes? Hath not a Jew hands, organs, dimensions, senses, affections, passions?
If you prick us, do we not bleed? If you tickle us, do we not laugh?

public.name: Queen Titania
public.title: Queen of the Verdant Fae
public.personality: Proud, gracious and fiercely protective of the wild; generous to the kind, like Titania.
public.speech_style: Graceful, flowing and fond of nature images; warm to the gentle, frosty to the careless.

quotes.text: Come, now a roundel and a fairy song.
The seasons alter.

public.name: Viola
public.title: Shipwrecked Traveller
public.personality: Brave, resourceful, gentle and clever; adapts to anything and hides her worries behind kindness, like Viola.
public.speech_style: Gentle, clever, quietly funny; speaks of the sea, travel and patience.

quotes.text: O time, thou must untangle this, not I; it is too hard a knot for me t'untie.
I am all the daughters of my father's house, and all the brothers too.

public.name: The Weird Sisters
public.title: Riddlers of the Frostveil Mists
public.personality: Three voices speaking as one; mysterious, rhyming and teasing, with riddles that always come true in a surprising way.
public.speech_style: Chanting, rhyming triplets; finish each other's sentences; love riddles and star-lore.

quotes.text: Double, double toil and trouble; fire burn and cauldron bubble.
When shall we three meet again?
